response.title: which projector screens can be put up without drilling into the wall
response.answer:
There are several types of projector screens that don't require drilling holes in your wall. Some stand on the floor, while others can be attached to existing structures.

For most homes and apartments, especially rentals, I'd recommend a floor-rising screen or a tripod screen.

5 types of no-drill projector screens
Shop

1. Floor-rising projector screen

Best for living rooms

Sits on the floor in a slim case and pulls upward. Some models are motorized. No wall or ceiling mounting needed.

Pros: Clean appearance, easy to hide when not in use.

Cons: More expensive than basic portable screens.

Shop

2. Tripod projector screen

Best budget option

A retractable screen supported by a tripod stand.

Pros: Affordable, portable, easy to set up.

Cons: Visible tripod legs and a less polished appearance.

Shop

3. Freestanding frame screen

A large screen stretched over a detachable frame with supporting feet.

Pros: Large viewing area, good screen tension.

Cons: Takes up floor space and may require assembly.

Shop

4. Tension-rod-mounted screen

A lightweight screen hung from a pressure-mounted rod between two suitable surfaces.

Pros: No floor stand, removable.

Cons: Requires a suitable opening and careful weight matching. Not appropriate for heavy retractable screens.

Shop

5. Adhesive-mounted fabric screen

Lightweight projection fabric attached using removable adhesive strips or hooks.

Pros: Very inexpensive, nearly invisible when removed.

Cons: Can wrinkle, adhesives may damage paint, and unsuitable for heavy screens.

Specific screens worth considering

121-inch motorized · Premium UST setup

$3,217.00

Motorized floor-rising screen designed for ultra-short-throw projectors.

One important consideration: if you have an ultra-short-throw (UST) projector, screen flatness and compatibility matter much more. A standard loose fabric screen may produce visible image distortion. 
BenQ US
+1

A quick question: Do you want a screen that stays up permanently without drilling, or one that you can put away after watching movies?

That makes a big difference in which type I'd recommend.
